moved.sentence: **Purpose-coherent groups are correctly scoped.** If every file in a candidate scope group has the same primary purpose, the group is coherent.

judged.note: should-keep-groups-purpose-coherent keeps the 'purpose-coherent groups are correctly scoped' claim, and the rationale keeps that same-primary-purpose files make a coherent group.

moved.sentence: Different purposes within the same group indicate either misclassification or a need to split.

judged.note: should-keep-groups-purpose-coherent keeps that differing purposes in one group indicate misclassification or a need to split.

moved.sentence: **Each scope group should have one sentence purpose.** Test: can you complete "This scope group exists to ___" with a single clear answer?

judged.note: should-have-one-sentence-purpose keeps the one-sentence purpose at SHOULD and its 'This scope group exists to ___' test, plus the 'and also' signal.

moved.sentence: **Mixed-purpose files mark the fault line.** A file that mixes UI and networking is a symptom — the fault line is between those two purposes.

judged.note: should-split-mixed-files-along-fault-line keeps the fault-line headline with the UI-and-networking example; the rationale keeps the symptom framing and where the fault line lies.

moved.sentence: Recommend splitting the file along that line.

judged.note: should-split-mixed-files-along-fault-line keeps recommending a split along the fault line (unkeyed, now SHOULD).

moved.sentence: **Configuration is rarely its own scope group.** Configuration files belong with the components they configure, unless they configure the entire application (in which case they belong in an application bootstrap scope group).

judged.note: should-place-configuration-with-its-components keeps placement with the configured components, the whole-application exception to a bootstrap group, and the rarely-its-own-group headline.

moved.sentence: **Testing infrastructure belongs adjacent to its subject.** Test mocks and fakes belong in the same scope group as the types they mock, or in a shared test infrastructure scope group if used across multiple groups.

judged.note: should-place-test-infrastructure-with-subject keeps mocks and fakes with the mocked types, or in shared test infrastructure when used across groups.

moved.sentence: **Build tooling is always its own scope group.** Build scripts, code generators, and Gradle/Webpack configuration are not part of any runtime scope group — they form a `Build Tooling` scope group that is excluded from runtime analysis.

judged.note: must-give-build-tooling-own-group keeps 'always its own group' at MUST, the three tooling kinds, not-runtime, and the Build Tooling group excluded from runtime analysis.
